summary: Union County, GA: 33 ft metal tower with a live-in cab, built 1949 per the register; listed as standing by Willhite, fenced and locked, houses radio equipment. Access accounts differ.

facts.design: 33-foot metal tower with a CL-100 series metal cab; 13 by 13 ft live-in cab with catwalk

access.note: Tower is fenced and its cab is locked. Register visit reports describe a gated, rutted access road. Willhite says the access road is the easiest way up.

visit.trail_note: Willhite describes an unmarked trail from Woody Gap that may overgrow. Register visit reports suggest hiking in because the road is gated.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Chattahoochee National Forest (Blue Ridge Ranger District)

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey team used the lookout as an azimuth mark, per Willhite
Lookout first appears on a 1938 map, per Willhite
Register gives 1949 as the construction year; a sign on the fence gives 1949 and credits the CCC
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on July 26, 2007
Register visit report of 25 November 2018: fenced, appears structurally sound, cab locked

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and sign both give 1949, but Willhite's 1935 survey reference and 1938 map show a lookout on the mountain earlier. The story gives 1949 as the register date and flags the earlier references.
Register visit reports say the road is gated and rutted and suggest hiking; Willhite says the access road is easiest. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Elevation not used. Register gives 3,114 ft (949 m), Willhite 3,720 ft, and the index 3,733 with no unit label; the brief's 1137.8 m comes from the index. Height of 33 ft converted to 10.1 m. Excluded a blog post titled 'A Day at Black Mountain Lookout Tower' (birding.mountainquailpress.com) because it describes a California tower. Willhite is a personal hiking site and the 1949 sign claim is second-hand. No Forest Service or post-2018 visit record was found; either would settle the access note. Status changed from unknown to standing on the register and Willhite evidence.
